title: Single-Step Anchor-Free Segment
statement: Let $x$ be a binary input and let $c,d$ be configurations of the dual transducer on $x$. If one step from $c$ reaches $d$ and $c$ is not in the anchor state, then the run from $c$ reaches $d$ after one step and does not visit the anchor state at any time strictly before then; hence it is an anchor-free segment of length $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ and $d$ are configurations of the dual transducer on a common binary input
$c$ is not in the anchor state
replaced:
Let $c$ and $d$ be configurations of the dual transducer such that one step takes $c$
to $d$ and $c$ is not in the anchor state. Then one step from $c$ reaches $d$ with no
anchor visit before it, i.e.\ $c$ to $d$ is an anchor-free segment of length $1$.
